name: Thyme
grown_as: Common garden thyme, a small evergreen shrub. The library also lists Wild thyme (in Britain Thymus drucei), a creeping mat with rounder leaves and purple-pink flowers; lemon and variegated thymes differ in colour. Drawn as garden thyme. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A low, dense, twiggy, evergreen bush 15 to 30 cm high, many thin, upright, woody stems, grey-brown and finely hairy.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite, in pairs, with tufts of smaller leaves in the joints, so the stems look crowded
leaf.outline: Tiny, narrowly oval to lance-shaped, 5 to 10 mm long and 1 to 3 mm wide
leaf.surface: Dotted with tiny glands, finely hairy beneath

flower.petals: Joined; a short upper lip and a three-lobed lower lip
flower.behind: A hairy, two-lipped calyx, often purple-tinged
flower.carried: In small dense rounded or short oblong heads at the shoot tips, sometimes with a separate ring just below
flower.size: 4 to 6 mm long; heads about 1 to 2 cm

fruit: Tiny brown nutlets in the dry calyces; the heads dry brown.
winter: Evergreen: a small grey-green bush, the leaves darker or purple-tinged in cold weather.

leaf: a tiny narrow leaf, under 1 cm
bloom: packed into a small rounded head
young: a small twiggy plant of thin stems crowded with tiny leaves
crop: a low dense twiggy bush, woody at the base
stems crowded with tiny grey-green leaves
flower: small rounded pale pink heads at the tips of almost every shoot
held just above the tiny leaves
seedhead: small dry brown heads on the shoot tips
dormant: the same small evergreen bush, leaves darker or purple-tinged

look_alikes: Wild thyme creeps flat in mats, with rounder leaves and deeper purple-pink flowers. Winter savory has longer, glossy, sharp-pointed leaves and flowers in the leaf joints. Oregano has broader soft leaves and flat-topped flower heads.
